entries.name: Bluesky (AT Protocol public API)

why.quote: Crawling the public parts of the API is allowed. HTTP 429 ("backoff") status codes are used for rate-limiting. Up to a handful concurrent requests should be ok.
why.basis: the API host's own robots.txt, which names crawling the public API as allowed; and the Terms of Service (https://bsky.social/about/support/tos, last updated 14 August 2025): "You retain ownership of your Content on the Bluesky application and website." (no reuse licence is given to others: each post stays its author's, so we store links and metadata only)

entries.interface: AT Protocol public XRPC API (public.api.bsky.app) and firehose; open by design per the register brief.
entries.notes: Read 18 Nov 2026 by data.b.collector@. Posts remain their authors' content under the Terms; we keep link and metadata only. Rate limits: https://docs.bsky.app/docs/advanced-guides/rate-limits (page is a client-side redirect; its text was not extractable).
entries.how: Bluesky public AppView API, no login: https://public.api.bsky.app/xrpc/app.bsky.feed.getAuthorFeed, app.bsky.feed.searchPosts and app.bsky.actor.getProfiles, with our named user agent, 2.5 s between requests, organisations' accounts only (register/social-accounts.json). Post text read in memory only to match topics and places; never stored. Each post shown by link, credited, licence "the platform's terms".

why.basis: the instance's terms (content stays its owner's; the licence given to the operator covers making content available "via one or more APIs for application access, via RSS") and https://mastodon.social/robots.txt, whose group for User-agent: * disallows only /media_proxy/, /interact/ and /api/v1/instance/domain_blocks

entries.interface: Public REST API and per-account RSS/Atom (.rss) on the instance; each instance sets its own rules.
entries.notes: Read 18 Nov 2026 by data.b.collector@. Other instances (e.g. masto.pt) have their own terms, not yet read: add each instance here before listing an account on it. Named AI-training agents are disallowed by robots.txt: we are a news data collector, not an AI-training crawler, and store no text.
entries.how: Mastodon public instance API, without credentials: /api/v1/accounts/lookup and /api/v1/accounts/:id/statuses (exclude_replies) on the instance of each listed organisation account (register/social-accounts.json; none yet), with our named user agent and 2.5 s between requests. Post text read in memory only; never stored. Each instance sets its own terms: the collector reads only instances whose terms were read, and mastodon.social's are the ones read so far.

As informações só devem ser utilizadas para fins pessoais, associativos ou profissionais; estando excluída toda a utilização para fins comerciais ou publicitários.

entries.interface: Decision lists on the website (HTML pages under /decisoes/: deliberacoes, autorizacoes, diretrizes, pareceres); no API or feed found.

Decisions can name organisations and people: link only, never copy text.

gives: country-level counts of exposed or vulnerable services and infections (dashboard)

why.quote: Non-Profit Research. You may perform research and analysis on a non-profit basis. ... Attribution. For published distribution other than the above Licensed Uses, attribution is required. ... you will not ... attempt to copy, reproduce, bundle, repackage, alter, modify, adapt, translate, ... or make derivative works based on the Restricted Content

entries.interface: Public dashboard (dashboard.shadowserver.org: connection reset when fetched); reports to network owners need registration.

Ask Shadowserver in writing (outreach@ drafts, a person sends) before any use. The dashboard itself could not be fetched, so its own terms are unread. Country dashboards are aggregates by design; never take network-owner reports (they list IPs).

gives: country and ASN routing, resource and visibility statistics

why.quote: A User may not re-package, compile, re-distribute the RIPEstat Service and any (or all) of the RIPEstat Data. entries.interface: RIPEstat Data API (stat.ripe.net/docs/02.data-api/): at most 1000 requests a day without a registered sourceapp, 8 concurrent requests per IP.
entries.notes: RESTRICTS: purpose is network analysis, monitoring, debugging and research (3.1); commercial derivatives need written permission from stat@ripe.net (a role address of the organisation; a person at PrompTugal would send the request). Research results must be attributed to RIPE NCC. Not-for-profit aggregate research may fit; lead to decide.

entries.name: IMPIC open data of the Portal BASE contracts (dados.gov.pt)
entries.owner: IMPIC, Instituto dos Mercados Públicos, do Imobiliário e da Construção
entries.how: the dataset's public API (https://dados.gov.pt/api/1/datasets/66d72d488ca4b7cb2de28712/) names the yearly file contratos<year>.zip; sources/base-gov-pt/collect.mjs downloads it when it has changed (updated weekly, about 70 MB), stream-parses it in memory and keeps the last 90 days of contracts whose contracting entity is the câmara of Lisboa or of an Algarve municipality, every 6 hours

terms.licence: Outra (Domínio Público), id other-pd, as the dataset's API states on 2026-11-18

entries.notes: dados.gov.pt/robots.txt answered with an HTML error page (HTTP 500) on 18 Nov 2026: no rule readable; only the documented dataset API and the file link are used, 2 to 3 requests a run. Contractors that are natural persons are shown as 'a natural person' (no name, no NIF, no object text). Same file PrompTugal__News__Civic reads (tools/extract-base.mjs); one collector, shared (Dinis, 18 Nov 2026).

why.quote: base.gov.pt not read (firewall)

entries.interface: None read. The same records are read from IMPIC's open data on dados.gov.pt (entry impic-dados-gov-pt); each contract links its own page on base.gov.pt, which we do not fetch.
entries.notes: No terms of use page of the portal was read. A request to IMPIC on the record would be drafted by outreach@ and sent by a person; not needed while the open data covers the need.
